title: Price of the Overage Weight (Cartwise Grocery Orders Glossary)
content:
# Price of the overage weight on lines sold by weight

Glossary entry, Cartwise Grocery Orders.

**Price of the overage weight** — the unit price at which the overage weight on a billed line sold by weight is valued for a weight-overage refund. It depends on how the billed unit price compares with the original unit price recorded on the line's billed entry:

- when the billed unit price is below the original unit price, the overage is priced at the original unit price;
- when the billed unit price is above the original unit price, the overage is priced at the average of the two prices;
- when the two prices are equal, the overage is priced at the billed unit price.

The price is used as it stands; it carries no rounding of its own, the weight-overage refund being rounded to the cent once.

## Reading the line

Both prices appear on the billed entry of the line sold by weight: the unit price billed, and the original unit price of the product originally ordered.

## Comparison table (hypothetical prices per pound)

| Original unit price | Billed unit price | Comparison | Price of the overage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.00 | 3.50 | billed below original | 4.00 (the original unit price) |
| 4.00 | 4.25 | billed above original | 4.125 (the average of 4.00 and 4.25) |
| 4.00 | 4.00 | equal | 4.00 (the billed unit price) |

## Basis Q&A

- **Which price applies when the store charged less per pound than the product originally ordered?** The original unit price.
- **Which price applies when the store charged more per pound?** The average of the billed and the original unit price, used without rounding.
- **And when the two are the same?** The billed unit price.
